name: Education and Learning
description: A flexible blueprint for learning material, curricula, pedagogy, competencies, assessment, and educational outcomes.

guidance: Define the learner, setting, prerequisites, intended outcomes, and assessment context before judging quality.
Distinguish curriculum intent, instructional method, learner activity, assessment evidence, and demonstrated outcome.
Trace concept and skill progression from prerequisites through practice, feedback, transfer, and mastery.
Evaluate alignment among outcomes, content, pedagogy, and assessment; do not infer learning from content coverage alone.
Represent accessibility, inclusion, cognitive demand, and learner variability where the evidence supports them.
Prefer concept maps and learning pathways for qualitative structure; chart only comparable outcomes or participation evidence.
State transfer limits, measurement validity, selection effects, and missing learner evidence explicitly.

sections.title: Learning Context and Core Answer
sections.purpose: Define who is learning what, under which conditions, and answer the educational objective directly.

blocks.title: Learning and Evidence Profile
instructions: Identify learners, setting, level, prerequisites, duration, delivery mode, outcomes, assessments, and coverage gaps when available.

blocks.title: Educational Summary
instructions: Answer the objective through intended learning, instructional approach, evidence of alignment or outcome, and the most consequential gap.
Do not equate exposure, completion, or satisfaction with learning.

blocks.title: Learning Design Findings
instructions: Present distinct findings about outcomes, sequence, pedagogy, practice, feedback, assessment, inclusion, or transfer.

sections.title: Concept and Skill Progression
sections.purpose: Explain how knowledge and capability are expected to develop and where the progression is strong or discontinuous.

blocks.title: Progression Analysis
instructions: Analyze prerequisites, conceptual dependencies, scaffolding, practice, feedback, increasing cognitive demand, and opportunities for transfer.
Do not invent learner mastery where only curriculum sequence is documented.

blocks.title: Learning Pathway
instructions: Map an evidence-backed path from prerequisite through instruction and practice to assessment or application; mark optional or missing stages.

sections.title: Outcome, Pedagogy and Assessment Alignment
sections.purpose: Test whether the learning outcomes, instructional experiences, and assessments measure the same intended capability.

blocks.title: Alignment and Learner Implications
instructions: Compare intended outcomes with taught content, learning activities, feedback, and assessment demands.
Separate design alignment from empirical effectiveness and discuss accessibility or learner variability only with evidence.

blocks.title: Comparable Learning Evidence

chart_slot.intent: Support one educational claim with comparable outcomes, participation, progression, or assessment evidence.

fallback.message: No comparable quantitative learning evidence is available.

instructions: Use consistent learner populations, assessment constructs, scales, and time windows; do not chart qualitative judgments as outcomes.

sections.title: Educational Evidence and Improvement
sections.purpose: Ground conclusions in curriculum, learner, assessment, or implementation evidence and identify conditional improvements.

blocks.title: Educational Evidence Trail
instructions: Tie findings to stated outcomes, activities, examples, assessments, learner results, feedback, or source locations.

blocks.title: Improvement Hypotheses
instructions: Frame improvements as testable hypotheses with the affected learner need, design change, implementation dependency, and evaluation signal.

sections.title: Learning Evidence Limits and Open Questions
sections.purpose: State what the available material cannot establish about learning quality, effectiveness, equity, or transfer.

blocks.title: Limitations and Unanswered Questions
instructions: Identify missing learner characteristics, baseline, comparison group, assessment validity, implementation fidelity, retention, transfer, accessibility, or outcome evidence only when material.
